statement: Pyramids which are of the same height and have polygonal bases are to one another as the bases.
heath_proof: Let there be pyramids of the same height of which the polygons ABCDE, FGHKL are the bases and the points M, N the vertices; I say that, as the base ABCDE is to the base FGHKL, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid FGHKLN. For let AC, AD, FH, FK be joined. Since then ABCM, ACDM are two pyramids which have triangular bases and equal height, they are to one another as the bases; [XII. 5] therefore, as the base ABC is to the base ACD, so is the pyramid ABCM to the pyramid ACDM. And, componendo, as the base ABCD is to the base ACD, so is the pyramid ABCDM to the pyramid ACDM. [V. 18] But also, as the base ACD is to the base ADE, so is the pyramid ACDM to the pyramid ADEM. [XII. 5] Therefore, ex aequali, as the base ABCD is to the base ADE, so is the pyramid ABCDM to the pyramid ADEM. [V. 22] And again componendo, as the base ABCDE is to the base ADE, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid ADEM. [V. 18] Similarly also it can be proved that, as the base FGHKL is to the base FGH, so is the pyramid FGHKLN to the pyramid FGHN. And, since ADEM, FGHN are two pyramids which have triangular bases and equal height, therefore, as the base ADE is to the base FGH, so is the pyramid ADEM to the pyramid FGHN. [XII. 5] But, as the base ADE is to the base ABCDE, so was the pyramid ADEM to the pyramid ABCDEM. Therefore also, ex aequali, as the base ABCDE is to the base FGH, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid FGHN. [V. 22] But further, as the base FGH is to the base FGHKL, so also was the pyramid FGHN to the pyramid FGHKLN. Therefore also, ex aequali, as the base ABCDE is to the base FGHKL, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid FGHKLN. [V. 22]
ai_proof_text:
12.6
**Statement:** Pyramids which are of the same height and have polygonal bases are to one another as the bases.

**Step 1.** Let there be two pyramids of the same height, the one with the polygonal base ABCDE and vertex M, the other with the polygonal base FGHKL and vertex N. I say that, as the base ABCDE is to the base FGHKL, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid FGHKLN.

**Step 2.** Join AC, AD, FH, FK [P1]. The polygon ABCDE is thereby divided into the triangles ABC, ACD, ADE, and the polygon FGHKL into the triangles FGH, FHK, FKL. (If the bases have more sides, join further diagonals from A and from F in the same way; the argument below is then repeated once for each additional triangle.)

**Step 3.** The solid constructed from the triangle ABC to the point M is a pyramid with triangular base [D11.12]; call it ABCM. Likewise ACDM, ADEM are pyramids with vertex M, and FGHN, FHKN, FKLN are pyramids with vertex N. The planes MAC, MAD cut the pyramid ABCDEM into the three pyramids ABCM, ACDM, ADEM, and the planes NFH, NFK cut the pyramid FGHKLN into the three pyramids FGHN, FHKN, FKLN; so each polygonal pyramid is the whole made up of its triangular pyramids, just as each polygonal base is the whole made up of its triangles.

**Step 4.** The height of a pyramid is the perpendicular drawn from its vertex to its base [D6.4]. The bases ABC, ACD, ADE all lie in the plane of ABCDE, and the pyramids ABCM, ACDM, ADEM all have the same vertex M; hence their height is one and the same perpendicular from M to that plane, namely the height of the pyramid ABCDEM. Similarly FGHN, FHKN, FKLN all have the height of FGHKLN. Since the pyramids ABCDEM and FGHKLN are of the same height by hypothesis, all six triangular pyramids are of the same height.

**Step 5.** Since ABCM and ACDM are pyramids of the same height with triangular bases, as the base ABC is to the base ACD, so is the pyramid ABCM to the pyramid ACDM [12.5].

**Step 6.** Componendo, as the base ABC together with ACD, that is the quadrilateral ABCD, is to the base ACD, so is the pyramid ABCM together with ACDM, that is the pyramid ABCDM, to the pyramid ACDM [5.18].

**Step 7.** Again, since ACDM and ADEM are pyramids of the same height with triangular bases, as the base ACD is to the base ADE, so is the pyramid ACDM to the pyramid ADEM [12.5].

**Step 8.** From Steps 6 and 7, ex aequali, as the base ABCD is to the base ADE, so is the pyramid ABCDM to the pyramid ADEM [5.22].

**Step 9.** Componendo, as the base ABCD together with ADE, that is the whole base ABCDE, is to the base ADE, so is the pyramid ABCDM together with ADEM, that is the whole pyramid ABCDEM, to the pyramid ADEM [5.18]. Thus, as the base ABCDE is to the triangle ADE, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid ADEM.

**Step 10.** In the same manner, applying 12.5 to the pairs FKLN, FHKN and FHKN, FGHN, then 5.18 and 5.22 as in Steps 5 to 9, it is shown that, as the base FGHKL is to the triangle FGH, so is the pyramid FGHKLN to the pyramid FGHN.

**Step 11.** Inversely, as the triangle FGH is to the base FGHKL, so is the pyramid FGHN to the pyramid FGHKLN [5.7 Por.].

**Step 12.** Since ADEM and FGHN are pyramids of the same height (Step 4) with triangular bases, as the triangle ADE is to the triangle FGH, so is the pyramid ADEM to the pyramid FGHN [12.5].

**Step 13.** From Steps 9 and 12, ex aequali, as the base ABCDE is to the triangle FGH, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid FGHN [5.22].

**Step 14.** From Steps 13 and 11, ex aequali, as the base ABCDE is to the base FGHKL, so is the pyramid ABCDEM to the pyramid FGHKLN [5.22].

**Step 15.** Therefore pyramids which are of the same height and have polygonal bases are to one another as the bases. Q.E.D.
